item.title: Information flow control in hybrid quantum networks
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Michael Siomau
arXiv:2611.07440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum resources can change the dynamical features and operational behaviors of conventional networks. Long-distance entanglement supports information transfer between nodes lacking a direct connection. This entanglement link not only modifies the stationary effective connectivity of the network but can also be used to suppress undesirable classical dynamics. By examining information flow control mechanism, we demonstrate that classical collective behavior can be well-balanced by altering the initially distributed entanglement. We show the entanglement thresholds for two distinct control approaches: linear response control and Lyapunov functional controllability.

item.title: Primitive Quantum Gates for an SU(3) Discrete Subgroup: Σ(216×3)
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Erik J. Gustafson, Henry Lamm, Edison Murairi, Sebastian Osorio Perez
arXiv:2611.08161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a primitive gate set for the digital quantum simulation of the 648-element discrete subgroup of SU(3), dsb. The five algorithmic primitives are the inversion, group multiplication, trace, group Fourier transform, and kinetic-phase gates, for which we provide qubit and qutrit--qubit decompositions. For a fiducial shear-viscosity calculation on a 10³ spatial lattice with 50 time steps and a total synthesis-error budget of 10⁻⁸, the estimated fault-tolerant costs are 2.3--6.8×10¹⁰ T gates in the qubit architecture and 1.3--5.9×10¹² R gates in the qutrit--qubit architecture.

item.description:

👤 Mu-En Liu, Andrea Zingarofalo, Victor Barizien, Jean-Daniel Bancal
arXiv:2611.06997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the minimal Bell scenario, all extremal quantum correlations are known, but the Tsirelson inequalities that delimit the quantum set remain poorly understood. We study which correlations can maximize a given Tsirelson inequality, and conversely, which inequalities are maximized by a given correlation. We show that every Tsirelson inequality with quantum advantage is maximized by a single, extremal correlation, and thus self-tests the corresponding realization. This characterizes all self-tests based on linear Bell inequalities in this scenario. We also show that at most a two-dimensional family of inequalities can be maximized by a nonlocal extremal correlation. arXiv:2611.08254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entropy has played a pivotal role in physics ever since its inception by Clausius in the early industrial age. Shannon ushered the concept into the information age by using it to describe fundamental limits of information processing, founding the field of information theory. Today, a fruitful interaction between information theory and physics is pushing our understanding of entropy forward. It has revealed, in particular, that no single notion of entropy suffices to capture all relevant properties of physical systems, making it necessary to consider a variety of entropic measures of quantum information, each with distinct features and uses. item.title: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Abhijat Sarma, Ruochen Ma, Cenke Xu
arXiv:2611.07017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that non-Abelian symmetry enrichment can protect a toric code memory against incoherent electric noise at any bond error probability pin[0,1]. For a toric code on the honeycomb lattice coupled to Sp(N) rotors, with electric anyons carrying the fundamental representation, we construct an efficient minimum-weight decoder whose logical error probability decays exponentially with system size for Nge40, a conservative sufficient bound. The same decoder also rules out strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in the fundamental channel of Sp(N) under the corresponding local decoherence in two dimensions. The construction extends to other symmetries, including SU(N).

item.title: Optimising physical parameters of a quantum network based on a loss-jitter trade-off
item.description:
📚 Quantum Science and Technology
👤 Marcus J Clark and Siddarth K Joshi
As quantum communication systems and networks are becoming a commercial reality, clarity on their future infrastructure is increasingly important. Based on the inevitable presence of some amount of loss, chromatic dispersion, and timing jitter, we present simulations to show that certain wavelengths and bandwidths have clear advantages.

item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yuanjie Ren, Margarita Davydova, Shankar Balasubramanian, Andreas Bauer
arXiv:2611.08488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.

item.title: Coupling between molecular exchange qubits
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Filippo Troiani, Jason S. R. McCoombs, Athanassios K. Boudalis
arXiv:2611.08058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin triangles are promising systems for defining and manipulating scalar degrees of freedom, such as chirality, partial spin sums, or combinations between the two. Here we extend this analysis to dimers formed by pairs of spin triangles, coupled by exchange or dipolar interactions. We show that the weak-coupling limit warrants the introduction of an effective two-qubit picture, and derive the expressions of the related Hamiltonians as a function of the underlying physical interaction between the triangles. We benchmark this two-qubit Hamiltonian against the microscopic one, and discuss the observable effects of the inter-triangle coupling on the spin-electric transitions between states with different chiralities or partial-spin sums.

item.description:

item.title: Bounding the entanglement of a state from its spectrum
item.description:
📚 Quantum
👤 Jofre Abellanet-Vidal, Guillem Müller-Rigat, Albert Rico, and Anna Sanpera
Quantum 10, 2260 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-06-2260 We introduce a framework to upper bound the entanglement content of a bipartite quantum state from its spectrum alone. Using linear maps and their inverses, we derive rigorous constraints on the maximal entanglement that can be activated under global unitary transformations. We use as entanglement quantifiers the negativity and the Schmidt number; however, our framework is general and applies to any other entanglement measure. Our approach yields compact analytical sufficient criteria for bounding the entanglement of full-rank states in arbitrary dimensions and reveals new spectral constraints on Schmidt number witnesses.
